title: Children and Youth Commission family survey findings
summary: At its September 21 meeting, the commission agreed to focus on building awareness of available behavioral health resources for youth and families, after a commissioner suggested the gap may be lack of awareness rather than lack of resources. The chair proposed an agenda item on annual survey reporting and a response goal. In August, the family survey ranked stable housing first, then mental health support and safe youth spaces.

timeline.text: The chair proposed an agenda item at the next meeting on annual survey reporting and a response goal.
Members discussed reporting survey results once a year or after reaching a set number of responses.
Members agreed to focus on building awareness of available resources.
A commissioner said the gap may be a lack of awareness of services, not a lack of resources.
The commission's community survey pointed to behavioral health supports for youth and families as a concern.
Community survey distribution update and results check-in: The family survey will stay on the agenda so commissioners can keep checking the data.
The vice chair will research what youth mental health resources are in place and report at the next meeting.
Under cost of living, households above 50,000 still named housing as a concern.
A commissioner said stable housing is ongoing and will take a very long time for families to achieve.
A commissioner said most people who completed the survey are from "out here on our side."
In the commission's family survey, stable housing was the top priority, followed by mental health support and safe youth spaces.
